Posted by John. R. Edwardson on Jun 9th, 2018 // No Comments
Dragon Financial & Investment Group LLC acquired a new stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) in the 4th quarter, according to the company in its most recent 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The fund acquired 2,731 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock, valued at approximately $462,000. Apple makes up approximately 0.4% of Dragon Financial & Investment Group LLC’s portfolio, making the stock its 15th biggest position.
Several other hedge funds and other institutional investors have also recently added to or reduced their stakes in the company. Mission Wealth Management LP grew its holdings in Apple by 1.1% during the fourth quarter. Mission Wealth Management LP now owns 81,556 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $13,802,000 after buying an additional 865 shares in the last quarter. Alexandria Capital LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 19.1% during the fourth quarter. Alexandria Capital LLC now owns 93,100 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $15,756,000 after buying an additional 14,942 shares in the last quarter. Sequoia Wealth Management LLC bought a new stake in Apple during the fourth quarter worth $239,000. Suffolk Capital Management LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 86.3% during the fourth quarter. Suffolk Capital Management LLC now owns 220,456 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $37,308,000 after buying an additional 102,091 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Vestpro Financial Partners Inc. dba CPF Texas bought a new stake in Apple during the fourth quarter worth $1,452,000. Hedge funds and other institutional investors own 58.14% of the company’s stock. Get Apple alerts:
Shares of NASDAQ AAPL opened at $191.70 on Friday. The stock has a market capitalization of $981.62 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 20.81, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.59 and a beta of 1.29. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a current ratio of 1.46. Apple has a twelve month low of $142.20 and a twelve month high of $194.20. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.69 by $0.04. The business had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The company’s quarterly revenue was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same period in the prior year, the company earned $2.10 EPS. research analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.42 EPS for the current fiscal year.
The company also recently disclosed a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Stockholders of record on Monday, May 14th were given a dividend of $0.73 per share. The ex-dividend date was Friday, May 11th. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a dividend yield of 1.52%. Apple’s dividend payout ratio is 31.70%.
Apple declared that its Board of Directors has approved a stock repurchase plan on Tuesday, May 1st that permits the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization permits the iPhone maker to repurchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock buyback plans are generally a sign that the company’s management believes its shares are undervalued.
Several equities research analysts recently issued reports on AAPL shares. Vetr downgraded Apple from a “strong-buy” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $187.18 price target for the company. in a report on Wednesday, February 14th. Raymond James reiterated a “market perform” rating on shares of Apple in a report on Friday, February 16th. BidaskClub upgraded Apple from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating in a report on Saturday, February 17th. ValuEngine upgraded Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a report on Thursday, March 1st. Finally, Rosenblatt Securities set a $180.00 price target on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday, March 7th. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty-one have given a buy rating and two have given a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. The stock has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $205.87.
In other news, COO Jeffrey E. Williams sold 15,653 shares of the stock in a transaction dated Tuesday, May 8th. The stock was sold at an average price of $185.18, for a total transaction of $2,898,622.54. Following the transaction, the chief operating officer now directly owns 168,181 shares in the company, valued at approximately $31,143,757.58. The sale was disclosed in a filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available through the SEC website . Also, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the stock in a transaction dated Tuesday, April 3rd. The shares were sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders have sold a total of 256,853 shares of company stock worth $45,378,566 over the last quarter. Corporate insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock.
Apple Company Profile
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
